answer: The scarecrows move every week, and the field hand counts the crows over each field, so the estate knows which rows the birds have spared. A prism scarecrow left standing for a month fails the rotation: the scarecrow must have moved at the dawn of the week, and a still scarecrow fools no crow at all. Faking a season of crow counts means hiring a field hand, moving forty scarecrows and paying 5,900, while the spiral book in the field hut is read at every harvest, so a field whose crows were never counted is left to the birds.
